sources.entry: Kamailio - Modular SIP server (registrar/proxy/router/etc). (Source Code) GPL-2.0 C/deb

summary.one_liner: Kamailio is an open source, scalable SIP signaling server that can act as a registrar, proxy, or router for VoIP, instant messaging, and presence.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Kamailio as an open source implementation of a SIP signaling server, based on the IETF SIP standard (RFC3261). It is aimed at large deployments such as IP telephony operators and carriers, and the README says it can also be used by enterprises or for personal VoIP, instant messaging, and presence. The README highlights flexibility, robustness, security, and a large feature set, but it does not list specific features in the text. It points to external documentation, a wiki, per-module READMEs, and an INSTALL file for setup. Development began in 2001 as SIP Express Router (SER) at Fraunhofer Fokus, was forked as OpenSER in 2005, and was renamed Kamailio in 2008 after the projects merged. The community now maintains it, and contributions go through GitHub pull requests and issues.
use_cases: operate SIP registrar and proxy for carriers
provide enterprise or personal VoIP service
handle instant messaging and presence over SIP
how_to_run: Follow the step-by-step source installation tutorials linked from the project website (not included in the README text).
Read the INSTALL file in the source code for build instructions.
Install Linux packages from the deb or rpm repositories linked in the README.
notable: Modular design with per-module documentation and READMEs
Descended from SIP Express Router (SER) and OpenSER, merged in 2008
Community-managed since Fraunhofer Fokus stepped back
Covers registrar, proxy, and router roles per the awesome-selfhosted listing
caveats: README does not include build or run commands; setup is delegated to external tutorials and the INSTALL file
Contributions to core and main modules require BSD licensing, with GPL code needing an OpenSSL linking exception
